_doc.purpose: End-to-end hard-overload evals. One simulated context window (default 64k, --context-window). Each case is an overload scenario: it names which LLM call it targets and pins a `size` in filler tokens that pushes that call past the window on legacy. Each case is a real multi-agent run (interaction agent -> workers -> callbacks -> reply) against an in-memory Gmail. Pass/fail = outcome judge on the final mailbox + replies; the rubric judge grades the trajectory. Legacy is expected to fail every scenario (that is the baseline); budgeted must survive the window AND still do the job well. Sweep mode (--sizes a,b,c) still works for curves but is not the default.

fields.history: conversation log seed; an item {"filler": true} marks where the conversation filler is inserted
fields.worker_logs: per-agent execution-log seed; an item {"filler": true} marks where the worker filler is inserted
fields.world: fake Gmail seed: emails (days_ago is converted to a date), drafts, contacts
fields.turns: user messages sent in order; each is sent only after the previous turn and all its worker callbacks have settled
fields.success: mechanical checks on the final mailbox and replies; shown as hints to the outcome judge and in the UI, no longer the verdict
fields.ideal_trajectory: reference for the trajectory judge only; never used for pass/fail
fields.extends: copy another case by id and override the listed fields
fields.filler_entry_tokens: size of each conversation filler entry (default 2000). ~300 makes the legacy count-based compaction fire from 40k up
fields.strip_worker_filler: drop worker-log filler markers from the extended case so only conversation compaction is exercised
fields.world.emails[].body: either text or {"generate": "contract_thread", "tokens": "size"|"size/3"|N} for a long generated thread; "size" ties the thread length to the grid size
fields.tier: "hard" and "disabled" cases are skipped unless --include-hard / named with --case
fields.expected: rubric judge thresholds: dispatches_max (question 14) and ideal_calls (question 16, limit is 2x)
fields.expected_outcome: plain-language end state the outcome judge grades against (it decides pass/fail; the `success` block is run as mechanical hints only)
fields.target: which LLM call(s) the scenario overflows: interaction_agent | summarizer | execution_agent | email_search | batch_payload | recall
fields.size: default filler size in tokens for this scenario (overridden by --sizes)
fields.baseline_note: expected legacy failure mode, for the write-up; not shown to any judge
fields.roster_generate: seed N decoy workers: {count, seed}. Names are topic+counterpart style; several near-duplicates of the real worker's name are included on purpose
fields.roster_age_days: per-worker last-used age in days for the case's real workers (default: recent); decoys are spread over the last 300 days

cases.name: fact_recall
cases.axis: soft overload: needle in conversation history
cases.description: A fact the user asked for earlier (Product X Q3 revenue = $2.4M) sits in the conversation log as a worker result, with near-miss distractors (Q2 figure, Product Y figure) right next to it. The user asks for the number again. Tests whether the agent can still surface the exact figure instead of re-deriving, guessing, or picking a distractor.

emails.body: Team, Q3 actuals are final. Product X revenue: $2.4M. Product Y revenue: $1.1M. Total: $3.5M. Detail deck attached to the shared drive.

emails.subject: Q2 revenue report
emails.body: Q2 actuals: Product X revenue $1.9M, Product Y revenue $0.9M. Total $2.8M.

emails.subject: Q3 marketing spend
emails.body: Q3 marketing spend came in at $0.6M, mostly on the Product X launch campaign.

history.content: pull the Q3 revenue numbers from the CFO's report and give me a quick summary
On it, checking the CFO's Q3 report now.

[SUCCESS] Finance Digest: Found 'Q3 revenue report' from cfo@company.com (thread thr-q3). Q3 actuals: Product X revenue $2.4M, Product Y revenue $1.1M, total $3.5M. For comparison, the Q2 report shows Product X at $1.9M and Product Y at $0.9M.
Q3 revenue: Product X $2.4M, Product Y $1.1M, total $3.5M. That's up from Q2 where Product X was $1.9M and Product Y $0.9M.
great, thanks
Anytime.

turns: what was Product X's Q3 revenue again?
cases.ideal_trajectory: Answer directly from history in one interaction-agent call, no dispatch. Acceptable but wasteful: dispatch Finance Digest to search email once and relay the result. Wrong: quoting $1.9M (Q2) or $1.1M (Product Y), or asking the user which report they mean.
cases.expected_outcome: The user is told Product X's Q3 revenue is $2.4M. Nothing is sent or drafted.
cases.baseline_note: History alone exceeds the window; 80 entries of 2k never reach the 110-entry count trigger, so legacy pastes all of it and the single interaction-agent request is rejected. User sees nothing (202 already returned).

cases.name: constraint_carry
cases.axis: soft overload: standing rule far back
cases.description: The user set a standing rule early on (always cc jordan@acme.com when emailing anyone at acme.com). The user then asks to email mike@acme.com and, after seeing the draft, says send it. Tests whether the rule survives the distance and is carried into the worker's instructions and into the actual sent mail.

emails.subject: Thursday sync agenda
emails.body: Hey, for Thursday's sync I'd like to cover the integration timeline and the open bugs list. Anything else?

history.content: new rule: whenever you email anyone at acme.com, always cc my assistant jordan@acme.com
Got it. I'll cc jordan@acme.com on every email to anyone at acme.com from now on.

turns: email mike@acme.com and ask if we can move Thursday's sync to Friday
looks good, send it
cases.ideal_trajectory: Turn 1: acknowledge, dispatch a worker (ideally the existing 'Acme Emails') with instructions that name mike@acme.com, the ask, and the cc to jordan@acme.com; worker creates one draft with the cc; callback shows the draft and asks for confirmation. Turn 2: dispatch the same worker to send that draft id; worker sends it; callback confirms to the user. Wrong: sent without the cc, cc only mentioned in the body text, a second draft, or sending before confirmation.
cases.expected_outcome: Exactly one email was sent to mike@acme.com asking to move Thursday's sync to Friday, with jordan@acme.com in the cc field (not merely mentioned in the body). It was sent only after the user's 'send it'. No stray drafts remain from the run. The user was shown the draft before confirming and told when it was sent.
cases.baseline_note: Interaction-agent prompt overflows on turn 1; the Acme Emails worker log (never compacted) also exceeds the window, so even a budgeted interaction agent cannot get the worker to run.

cases.name: prior_result_reuse
cases.axis: soft overload: reuse an existing draft from a bloated worker
cases.description: A draft to Sarah (draft-7781 on thread thr-contract) was already created by the 'Email to Sarah' worker and shown to the user. The user says send it. Tests whether the system reuses the existing worker and existing draft instead of re-drafting from scratch or losing the draft id.

drafts.body: Hi Sarah, legal is reviewing the contract now and we expect to send redlines back by Friday. Thanks for your patience.

Drafting that reply to Sarah now.

[SUCCESS] Email to Sarah: Created draft draft-7781 on thread thr-contract. to: sarah@acme.com, subject: Re: Contract status?, body: Hi Sarah, legal is reviewing the contract now and we expect to send redlines back by Friday. Thanks for your patience.

Here's the draft to Sarah — subject 'Re: Contract status?': "Hi Sarah, legal is reviewing the contract now and we expect to send redlines back by Friday. Thanks for your patience." Want me to send it?

Email to Sarah.content: Reply to sarah@acme.com on her 'Contract status?' thread (thr-contract): legal is reviewing the contract and we will send redlines back by Friday. Create the draft only; do not send.

Calling gmail_create_draft with: {"recipient_email": "sarah@acme.com", "subject": "Re: Contract status?", "thread_id": "thr-contract", "body": "Hi Sarah, legal is reviewing the contract now and we expect to send redlines back by Friday. Thanks for your patience."}

Created draft draft-7781 on thread thr-contract. to: sarah@acme.com, subject: Re: Contract status?, body: Hi Sarah, legal is reviewing the contract now and we expect to send redlines back by Friday. Thanks for your patience.

turns: yes, send the Sarah email
cases.ideal_trajectory: Dispatch the existing 'Email to Sarah' worker with 'send draft draft-7781'; worker calls gmail_execute_draft(draft-7781); callback confirms to the user. Two interaction-agent turns, one worker run, one tool call. Acceptable but wasteful: worker lists drafts first to find the id. Wrong: creating a new draft, sending a new email instead of the existing draft, asking the user to confirm again, or a new worker that does not know the draft exists.
cases.expected_outcome: The existing draft draft-7781 to sarah@acme.com was sent (one send, no new draft created). The user was told it was sent.
cases.baseline_note: Same shape as E2E-02 with the needle (draft-7781) in the worker log; worker overflow forces budgeted to spawn a fresh worker that has no memory of the draft.

cases.name: search_synthesis
cases.axis: soft overload: search with distractors from a bloated worker
cases.description: The 'Finance Emails' worker already has a long log of unrelated past searches. The mailbox holds the Q3 actuals ($2.4M for Product X) next to distractors: the Q2 actuals ($1.9M), a Q3 forecast ($2.1M) and a marketing-spend mail. The user asks for the actual Q3 revenue. Tests whether a worker with a bloated log still searches well, reads the right mail, and the interaction agent relays the right number.

emails.body: Team, Q3 actuals are final. Product X revenue: $2.4M. Product Y revenue: $1.1M. Total: $3.5M.

emails.subject: Product X Q3 forecast
emails.body: Forecast for Product X Q3 revenue is $2.1M assuming the launch lands in August.

emails.subject: Q2 revenue report

Morning! What can I do for you?

turns: find the actual Q3 revenue for Product X in my email and tell me the number
cases.ideal_trajectory: Acknowledge, dispatch the 'Finance Emails' worker to search for the Q3 revenue report; worker runs one or two searches, picks the CFO actuals over the forecast and Q2 mails, reports $2.4M; callback relays $2.4M. Wrong: relaying $2.1M (forecast) or $1.9M (Q2), answering without searching, or looping through many near-identical searches.
cases.expected_outcome: The user is told the actual Q3 revenue for Product X is $2.4M (not the $2.1M forecast or the $1.9M Q2 figure). Nothing is sent or drafted.

cases.name: multi_step_reply
cases.axis: trajectory: search, draft on the right thread, confirm, send
cases.description: Sarah has several threads; the newest is about revised contract terms. The user asks to find that latest email and draft a reply accepting the revised terms, then confirms send. This is the longest legitimate chain in the suite (search, draft on the correct thread, callback, confirm, send, callback) and is where step-count inflation and loops show up.

emails.subject: Contract - revised terms
emails.body: Hi, following our call, here are the revised terms: net-45 payment, 2% early-payment discount, 12-month initial term. Let me know if you accept and I'll get the paperwork moving.

emails.subject: Contract status?
emails.body: Any update on where the contract stands on your side?

emails.subject: Lunch next week?
emails.body: Are you free for lunch next Tuesday or Wednesday?

history.content: hey
Hey! What do you need?

turns: find Sarah's latest email about the revised contract terms and draft a reply saying we accept the revised terms
send it
cases.ideal_trajectory: Turn 1: acknowledge, dispatch 'Email to Sarah' to find the latest revised-terms email and draft a reply on that thread; worker searches once, creates one draft with thread_id thr-revised, reports the draft; callback shows the draft and asks to confirm. Turn 2: dispatch the same worker to send that draft; worker sends; callback confirms. Wrong: replying on the 'Contract status?' or lunch thread, a fresh email with no thread, repeated searches, a second draft, or sending before confirmation.
cases.expected_outcome: Exactly one reply was sent to sarah@acme.com on the revised-terms thread (thr-revised) saying we accept the revised terms, sent only after the user's 'send it'. No stray drafts remain. The user saw the draft before confirming.
cases.baseline_note: Longest chain; both prompts overflow on legacy. On both strategies the worker tends to gmail_reply_to_thread (sends immediately) instead of drafting — a tool-design gap independent of overload.

cases.name: compaction_fact_recall
cases.axis: compaction: needle folded into the summary
cases.description: Same scenario as E2E-01 (Product X Q3 revenue answered earlier, next to Q2 and Product Y distractors), but the filler is many small 300-token chat entries instead of few large ones. From 40k up the legacy count-based compaction (100 entries + 10 tail) fires and the needle is folded into the summary, so this tests whether the exact figure survives summarization rather than whether the raw history fits.
cases.ideal_trajectory: Answer $2.4M directly from the conversation summary (or, under budgeted, recall the original entry) in one call. Wrong: a distractor figure, re-deriving via a worker when the summary already states it, or asking which report.
cases.baseline_note: 300-token entries: the 110-entry count trigger fires repeatedly. With 160k of filler the tail is 540 entries; each 100-entry batch is ~30k so legacy compaction succeeds here, and the needle is folded into the summary. Tests summary fidelity.

cases.name: compaction_constraint_carry
cases.axis: compaction: standing rule folded into the summary
cases.description: Same scenario as E2E-02 (standing rule: cc jordan@acme.com on every Acme email), with 300-token conversation filler so legacy compaction fires and the rule only survives if the summarizer keeps it. Worker-log filler is removed so the cell isolates conversation compaction. Two turns: email Mike, then send it.
cases.baseline_note: Standing cc rule folded into the summary by legacy compaction; pass depends on the summarizer keeping it.

cases.name: compaction_prior_result
cases.axis: compaction: draft id folded into the summary
cases.description: Same scenario as E2E-03 (draft-7781 to Sarah already exists and was shown to the user), with 300-token conversation filler so legacy compaction folds the draft callback into the summary. Worker-log filler removed. Tests whether the draft id and the fact that a draft exists survive summarization and are reused.
cases.baseline_note: Draft id folded into the summary by legacy compaction.

cases.name: long_thread_decide_reply
cases.axis: big entry: long tool result, then a decision that depends on it
cases.description: The mailbox holds one very long negotiation thread with Sarah whose length equals the grid size, with five specific terms spread through it (net-45, 2% discount, 12-month term, $500k liability cap, 60-day renewal notice). No conversation filler. Turn 1 asks for a summary: the worker's search result is one huge tool payload that no compaction can touch, and its summary comes back into the conversation log as one large entry. Turn 2 makes a decision that requires the thread's content (accept net-45 and the discount, push the liability cap to $1M) and turn 3 sends. Tests the worker path under a single oversized observation and the interaction agent's handling of one oversized entry.

emails.subject: Lunch next week?
emails.body: Are you free for lunch next Tuesday or Wednesday?

Hey! What do you need?

turns: summarize the contract negotiation thread with Sarah for me — I need the key terms each side is at
ok. reply to Sarah on that thread: we accept net-45 and the 2% early-payment discount, but we need the liability cap raised to $1M
send it
cases.ideal_trajectory: Turn 1: dispatch 'Email to Sarah' to find and summarize the negotiation thread; one search; the summary lists all five terms; callback relays them. Turn 2: dispatch the same worker to draft a reply on thread thr-nego stating acceptance of net-45 and the 2% discount and asking for a $1M liability cap; one draft with thread_id thr-nego; callback shows it and asks to confirm. Turn 3: send that draft; callback confirms. Wrong: a summary missing the liability cap or renewal notice (partial read), a fresh email off-thread, terms invented, a second draft, or sending before turn 3.
cases.expected_outcome: Turn 1: the user got a summary naming the key terms from the thread (net-45, 2% early-payment discount, 12-month term, $500k liability cap, 60-day renewal notice). Turn 2/3: exactly one reply was sent to sarah@acme.com on thread thr-nego accepting net-45 and the 2% discount and asking for the liability cap to be raised to $1M, sent only after 'send it'. No stray drafts remain.
cases.baseline_note: The fetched thread (160k) lands in the email-search sub-agent's messages and then in the worker's messages; neither strategy bounds tool results mid-run. Expected to fail on both — Issue 2 evidence.

cases.name: multi_thread_status_email
cases.axis: hard: synthesize several long threads into one drafted email
cases.description: Three long negotiation threads with three different companies (Acme, Globex, Initech), each one third of the size, with different terms in each (Acme net-45/$500k, Globex net-60/$750k, Initech net-30/$1M). The user asks for a status email to their boss covering all three, then sends it. The worker must search, read all three long payloads, and the draft must carry the right pair of figures for each company. Skipped by default; run with --include-hard once the weaker cases pass.

history.content: hey
Hey! What do you need?

turns: draft an email to my boss boss@company.com with a status update on the Acme, Globex and Initech negotiations — for each one, where payment terms and the liability cap currently stand
send it
cases.ideal_trajectory: Turn 1: dispatch one worker to search the three threads, read each, and draft one email to boss@company.com with a per-company section naming payment terms and liability cap; callback shows the draft. Turn 2: send it. Wrong: a draft missing a company, terms attributed to the wrong company (each company has different figures), several drafts, or sending before confirmation.
cases.expected_outcome: Exactly one email was sent to boss@company.com with a status section for each of Acme, Globex and Initech stating that company's payment terms and liability cap (Acme net-45 / $500k, Globex net-60 / $750k, Initech net-30 / $1M), sent only after 'send it'. No stray drafts remain.
cases.baseline_note: Three threads totalling the window; hard tier.

cases.name: compaction_batch_overflow
cases.axis: hard overload: the summarizer call itself
cases.description: Conversation filler of 120 entries of 1.5k tokens. The 110-entry count trigger fires, and legacy folds 100 entries in one summarizer call: ~145k tokens, over a 64k window. The compaction fails and, because the same batch is retried on every append, stays failed forever; the raw tail is then pasted whole into the interaction agent. Budgeted caps each summarizer batch at 60k and bounds each entry. The needle (Product X Q3 = $2.4M) sits before the filler.
cases.baseline_note: Legacy: summarizer request blocked; every later summarize attempt blocks again; interaction-agent prompt (~180k) also blocked. Two distinct overflow points in one cell.
cases.ideal_trajectory: Compaction succeeds in bounded batches; the agent answers $2.4M from the summary or via recall_history in one or two calls.

cases.name: batch_payload_overflow
cases.axis: hard overload: merged worker callback in the current-turn slot
cases.description: The user asks for five things at once, each handled by a different worker. Each company's thread has different terms (Acme net-45/$500k, Globex net-60/$750k, Initech net-30/$1M, Umbrella net-90/$250k, Hooli net-15/$2M) and each worker's final response is long (each thread is ~30k tokens), and the batch manager merges all five into ONE agent message for the callback turn. That message sits in the current-turn slot, which no strategy bounds today. Tests whether the interaction agent can still relay five results.
cases.baseline_note: Both strategies likely overflow on the callback turn: the merged payload is outside the history budget. Expected finding, not a pass.

cases.name: giant_entry
cases.axis: hard overload: one oversized conversation entry
cases.description: The user pasted an entire 80k-token negotiation thread into the chat earlier (one conversation entry) and asked for a summary, which was given. A few normal turns later they ask a specific question about it (the liability cap). Legacy re-sends the 80k entry verbatim on every turn until 100 more entries arrive. Budgeted previews it and recalls on demand.
cases.baseline_note: Legacy: every interaction-agent request exceeds the window; silent failure. Budgeted: preview + recall_history with offset paging (the entry is larger than the 6k recall cap, so the agent must page or search).

cases.name: recall_overflow
cases.axis: hard overload: the recall tool's own output
cases.description: Five earlier worker results of ~16k tokens each (five long thread summaries) sit in history as five entries, all previewed under the budget. The user asks for a figure that appears only in the fourth one. A naive recall of all five ids is 80k tokens; the recall cap (6k) must page or the agent must search instead. Tests that the fix does not have its own overflow hole.
cases.baseline_note: Legacy: 80k of history pasted whole, blocked on the first call; a normal overflow baseline. Budgeted: must use recall_history with a query or paging without exceeding the window — tests that the fix has no overflow hole of its own.

cases.name: verbatim_send_by_pointer
cases.axis: verbatim: send a huge pasted text exactly, without passing it through a model
cases.description: The user pasted a ~70k-token thread earlier and now asks to email that whole text to sarah@acme.com exactly as pasted, then confirms send. The text must reach the sent email verbatim: no model can hold it, so the only correct path is by reference (the conversation entry id), resolved server-side into the draft body. Five distinctive sentences sit at 5%..95% of the text; the sent body must contain all of them.
cases.baseline_note: Legacy: blocked at 64k. Budgeted before body_from: the agent either digests the text (a summary is sent, not the text) or pages it and overflows.

cases.name: multi_entry_synthesis
cases.axis: synthesis across several large entries at once
cases.description: Five worker reports, each a full ~25k-token negotiation thread for a different company with different terms, sit in history as five entries (125k total). The mailbox is empty.
